summary: A franchise owner says the raise adds up fast and his own hours grow to cover it.
realLife: A family that ran three fast-food stores said a state wage step for the industry would cost a few thousand dollars per store each month and hundreds of thousands a year. They said the trade was being singled out, cut worker hours to the minimum and put the owner on a long run of days with no day off. An economist in the same story expected all rivals to raise prices together and keep customers.
sources: CBS News Bay Area (San Jose, California), 'Fast food franchise owners, workers see $20 hourly wage increase with some concern', April 1, 2024: https://www.cbsnews.com/amp/sanfrancisco/news/fast-food-franchise-owners-workers-see-20-hourly-wage-increase-with-some-concern
